From Figure 1, we are given:
- Magnitude of Resultant Force, $R = 500\text{ N}$, directed along the positive y-axis ($	heta_R = 90^\circ$).
- One force is $F_1 = 700\text{ N}$ acting at an angle of $15^\circ$ below the negative x-axis (or $180^\circ + 15^\circ = 195^\circ$, or components: $-700 \cos 15^\circ \hat{i} - 700 \sin 15^\circ \hat{j}$). Let's assume standard angles from the figure: $700\text{ N}$ is at $15^\circ$ to the left of the negative x-axis.
- The second force is $F$ acting at an angle $\theta$ with the positive x-axis.

**Step 1: Write Equilibrium Equations for Components**
$$\sum F_x = R_x \implies -700 \cos(15^\circ) + F \cos\theta = 500 \cos(90^\circ) = 0$$
$$F \cos\theta = 700 \cos(15^\circ) = 700 \times 0.9659 = 676.13\text{ N} \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

$$\sum F_y = R_y \implies -700 \sin(15^\circ) + F \sin\theta = 500 \sin(90^\circ) = 500$$
$$-700 \times 0.2588 + F \sin\theta = 500$$
$$-181.16 + F \sin\theta = 500$$
$$F \sin\theta = 500 + 181.16 = 681.16\text{ N} \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

**Step 2: Determine Magnitude of Force $F$**
$$F = \sqrt{(F \cos\theta)^2 + (F \sin\theta)^2} = \sqrt{(676.13)^2 + (681.16)^2}$$
$$F = \sqrt{457151.7 + 463978.9} = \sqrt{921130.6} = 959.76\text{ N}$$-

**Step 3: Determine Direction $\theta$**
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{F \sin\theta}{F \cos\theta}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{681.16}{676.13}\right) = \tan^{-1}(1.0074) = 45.21^\circ$$
proTip: Always resolve inclined forces into standard horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components using proper trigonometric signs.
